This bill is part of a package that creates the Medicare Guarantee Fund.
The fund would have special accounts from which Medicare and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme payments would be made automatically.
Mechanisms to top up the accounts are included so that underestimated liabilities do not interrupt payments.
Establishes the Medicare Guarantee Fund with special accounts in Treasury and Health portfolios.
Requires that from 1 July 2017 or later, MBS and PBS payments be automatically debited from the Health special account.
Makes the Treasurer credit the Treasury special account each year with an amount matching estimated liabilities and shift that sum to the Health special account.
Creates procedures to handle overestimates and shortfalls, including topping up the Health special account.

The motion asked for this bill to be withdrawn and redrafted *"to provide actual guarantees for the future of Medicare"*. ### What do these bills do? If passed, the [bills](http://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r5900) will create the Medicare Guarantee Fund. The Fund will be used to fund both Medicare benefits and payments under the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme [**PBS**]. The creation of this fund is a response to the 2016 election, which the Labor Party accused the Coalition of wanted to privatise Medicare. The [bills digest](http://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd1617a/17bd108) emphasises that these bills don't *"guarantee the continuing existence of Medicare of itself ... The MP moved the Medicare Guarantee (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2017, which amends the Health Insurance Act 1973 and National Health Act 1953 to replace existing special appropriations for the MBS and PBS with a Medicare Guarantee Fund, aiming to increase transparency and secure funding for these schemes.

The speaker argued the Medicare Guarantee Bill 2017 is an accounting trick by the Abbott-Turnbull government to mask its history of attacking Medicare, which Labor created in 1984 and which the Coalition opposed; Labor will not oppose the bill but will highlight the government's hypocrisy, and demands the immediate unfreezing of the Medicare Benefits Schedule.

The Medicare Guarantee Bill is a gimmick and an accounting trick that provides no real guarantee of funding or protection from future cuts, merely changing how funds are appropriated without locking in Medicare or PBS spending. The speaker argued the bill offers only "visibility" of costs, not a safeguard, and accused the government of undermining Medicare despite election promises to protect it.

The Medicare Guarantee Bill was defended as improving transparency in how Medicare is funded, with opposition support noted. The government’s $1.2 billion budget commitment to more medicines on the PBS was also highlighted, while opposition scare campaigns were dismissed.

The speaker argued that the Medicare Guarantee Bill 2017 establishes a Medicare Guarantee Fund to secure ongoing funding for the Medicare Benefits Schedule and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme from 1 July 2017, with an estimated $33.8 billion credited in the next financial year, including $12.1 billion from the Medicare levy.

The speaker argued the Medicare Guarantee Bill is a meaningless accounting trick that does not protect Medicare, citing the government's $2.2 billion freeze on patient rebates, cuts to public hospitals, and only 67% of urgent emergency patients seen within 30 minutes. They proposed amendments to include public hospital funding, immediate indexation of frozen rebates, and reinvestment of savings from the Medicare Benefits Schedule Review.

The speaker argued that the Medicare Guarantee Bill 2017 is a deceptive "fig leaf" that does not genuinely protect Medicare, and called for an end to the freeze on the Medicare Benefits Schedule. They cited a GP bulk-billing rate of 68.1% in their electorate of Griffith, ranking 141st out of 150 electorates, and claimed that up to 13,000 people in the electorate delay seeing a doctor as a result.
